Research in construction plays an important part in the solution to complex global problems—from sustainability and climate change to digital transformation and equitable urbanism. Regardless of whether you are studying civil engineering, architecture, or construction management, these dissertation titles demonstrate progressive issues facing the industry such as green materials, AI factors, smart cities, and regulatory frameworks. Each of these themes prepares you to engage substantive practice and to add to the body of knowledge in the construction industry. Review the following list for inspiration for your dissertation topic in Construction!

1. The Use of Renewable Energy Systems in Sustainable Design and Development

Focus: Investigate the use of solar PV, wind, or geothermal energy systems – what is the cost for the new construction, how do they perform, and what are the carbon reduction benefits of those systems.

2. Barriers to Sustainable Construction in Emerging Economies

Focus: A comparative qualitative study of the barriers to sustainable construction in Ghana and Saudi Arabia – covers policy barriers, restricted access to sustainable materials, and barriers to sustainable construction infrastructure.

3. Life-Cycle Assessments of Sustainable Building Materials

Focus: Conduct Project Life Cycle Assessments of industrial by-products (i.e. fly ash, slag) and bio-based binders (i.e. algae, hempcrete) to consider strength, cost, and impact on the environment at the very earliest of Project Life Cycle Assessments.

4. Uses of Generative AI for Design and Document Management in Construction

Focus: Examination of how LLMs and RAG frameworks can automate design-related inquiries of construction contracts and generate drafts of contracts and proceeds with project coordination.

5. Smart Construction Management - BIM and IoT

Focus: Explore the benefits of Building Information modelling, digital twins, and building IoT Project Monitoring (sensor) systems for energy efficiency, safety and operational decisions in real time.

6. Adoption of Circular Economy Practices/Principles in Construction Waste Management

Focus: Understanding the use of reuse, recycling and digitalisation (e.g. blockchain and smart contracts) as tools to mitigate the amount of construction waste that goes to landfill and advance building sustainability.

7. Agile and Lean Construction Techniques in delivery of infrastructure projects

Focus: Utilising components of the Toyota Production System (e.g., real time scheduling, prefabrication) to increase productivity and reduce waste on construction sites.

8. Prefabrication & Modular Construction Techniques for Affordable Housing

Focus: Examining efficiency, cost and regulatory matters related to establish a modular building system in urban and rural settings.

9. Climate-adaptive, Disaster Resilient Urban Infrastructure in Flood-Prone Cities

Focus: Assessing design strategies, enduring construction standards, and cost-benefit outcomes for climate-adaptive buildings and infrastructure.

10. Regulatory Influences on Sustainable Construction in Hybrid Economies

Focus: A comparative analysis of the influences of regulatory instruments on green building in a country like Nigeria. Analysis of policy effectiveness (perceived and actual) and legislation implementation.
